title: add high-resolution perf counters and speedscope timeline export for runtime profiling
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: We need finer-grained, low-overhead telemetry inside the serving runtime to troubleshoot kernel hotspots, KV-cache behavior, and continuous-batching effects under production traffic. This PR adds high-resolution software counters, a lightweight timeline exporter compatible with speedscope/Chrome trace, and small microbench hooks used by perf lab runs. Goals: (1) incrementally instrument critical code paths (kernel dispatch, kernel completion, KV get/set, batch coalescing, KV cache hit/miss), (2) expose an in-process counter API usable from C++ and Rust components, (3) produce compact timeline JSONs for per-request traces and aggregate traces for benchmarking, (4) add CI perf-bench job that validates instrumentation does not regress tail latency beyond a small epsilon. Changes shipped: new PerfCounter API (C++ header + small ring buffer), per-thread timeline spans, userland export script (tools/perf/trace_to_speedscope.py), microbenchmark harness additions for kernel microbench and KV-cache microbench, and docs with examples and dashboard generation snippets. Checklist: - [x] Add PerfCounter and TimelineSpan primitives - [x] Instrument kernel dispatch and completion hooks - [x] Increment KV-cache hit/miss counters and prefix statistics - [x] Add continuous-batching sampling hooks and batch-size histogram - [x] Add trace exporter and speedscope compatibility - [x] Add unit tests for counter roll-over and ring-buffer concurrency - [x] Add small perf CI job (smoke) - [x] Update runtime docs and perf dashboard generation notes Implementation notes: PerfCounter is implemented as a cacheline-aligned 64-bit counter with relaxed atomic updates and per-core aggregation to reduce contention. Timeline spans are sampled (configurable rate) to avoid blow-up in production; the exporter collapses adjacent spans with identical tags. The trace exporter supports both per-request single-trace mode and aggregated microbench mode. Backwards compatibility: feature guarded by a runtime flag (--enable-highres-profiler) and default sampling rate is conservative. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1089/high-res-profiler (internal), speedscope: https://www.speedscope.app/ , perf lab: README at tools/perf/README.md

Instrument kernel_dispatch and kernel_complete hooks (A. Raman)
Add KV cache counters and continuous-batch sampling (A. Raman)
Add trace exporter and python conversion tool (A. Raman)
Perf CI job + dashboard generation snippet (A. Raman)

diff_snippets: +++ services/runtime/src/profiler/perf_counter.h: added PerfCounter class with per-core buckets and increment_if_enabled() inline;
+++ services/runtime/src/scheduler/kernel_dispatch.cc: around dispatch - emit TimelineSpan::start("kernel_dispatch", kernel_id) and TimelineSpan::end();
+++ services/runtime/src/cache/kv_cache_metrics.cc: increment(kv_get_hits) on positive lookup, increment(kv_get_misses) on miss; added prefix_hit_histogram update;

+++ tools/perf/trace_to_speedscope.py: reads newline-delimited compact traces, collapses identical adjacent spans and emits speedscope JSON with shared frames; usage: tools/perf/trace_to_speedscope.py input.ndjson > out.speedscope.json
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: The per-core bucket allocation looks good but needs an amortized memory estimate in the docs. Can we bound worst-case memory if sampling rate is high?
Aisha Raman: Added a note in docs/runtime/profiling.md with a formula for memory usage and default caps. Sampling rate defaults to 1/1000; documented tradeoffs.
Priya Desai: In kernel_dispatch path the inline start/end looks expensive at hot paths; can we make it zero-cost when disabled?

Aisha Raman: start/end are guarded by a compile-time fast-path (unlikely branch) and become no-op if --enable-highres-profiler is false. Bench numbers added to microbench show <0.2% overhead when disabled.
Marco Alvarez: Trace exporter should redact request payloads by default. Please add a redact config.
Aisha Raman: Added redact=true default and config flag --profiler-redact-payloads; updated exporter tests.
Priya Desai: Please add a small Windows shim or skip on non-posix in trace_to_speedscope.py; CI failed on runner with no /proc/self/cpuinfo.
Aisha Raman: Updated script to use psutil fallback and added test guards. CI perf-smoke job re-run passed.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after minor doc tweak.
release_notes:
- Added high-resolution PerfCounter API and per-thread timeline spans to the serving runtime.
- Added speedscope-compatible trace exporter and tools/perf/trace_to_speedscope.py.
- Instrumented kernel dispatch/completion, KV-cache hit/miss counters, and continuous-batching sampling hooks.
- New perf-smoke CI job to ensure instrumentation overhead remains small.
Notes: Feature is disabled by default; enable with --enable-highres-profiler. Default sampling is conservative to avoid trace blow-up.
